question.problem:
$$
{U}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{10} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{10}\end{aligned}],\,{V}_{r}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
question.worked_solution:
If $A={U}_{r}{Σ}_{r}{V}_{r}^{T}$ is a reduced singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
{V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}_{r}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of ${Σ}_{r}.$

First, notice that

$$
{Σ}_{r}^{+}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{U}_{r}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={V}_{r}\,{Σ}_{r}^{+}\,{U}_{r}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
